title: ENIAC, an early general-purpose electronic computer
summary: ENIAC was an all-electronic digital computer built at the University of Pennsylvania's Moore School for the US Army. Work began in 1943 and it was completed by February 1946. Designed for artillery range tables, it was used for hydrogen bomb calculations and ran far faster than electromechanical machines.

as_recorded.value: work began in early 1943 on ENIAC

importance.justification: Described as the first programmable general-purpose electronic digital computer, a milestone in computing history.
